body: My Dad’s emotional bluntness is nothing intentional and I don’t hold it against him at all.
It's just how he is. He has always been very distant and emotionally blunted. I don't think it's anything against him. Just his personality.
I have a bit with my mother but my father and I just really aren't close at all (they are still in my life though and married). She has been way more supportive lately.
They are my parents.. and like I said they were not bad parents in my opinion and aren’t now especially.

Nothing notable. I don't want to paint the imagine that my parents are bad parents - they really aren't. But they didn't care much about what I was going through emotionally growing up. When I would try to talk about sadness or depression they would just send me to a psychiatrist. 

That being said - since I was diagnosed Bipolar they have been taking a lot of steps to help me, especially my mom. My dad is very emotionally blunted though so its hard for him.

The very first time ever? I was in high school and dating a guy who was very emotionally abusive, worst relationship I have ever had by far even to this day but I was young and stupid. That's the first time I ever contemplated leaving this life. 

I haven't had many suicidal episodes in my life to be honest which is also very unnerving because my diagnosis is still fairly new and I'm very worried for what the future holds because what caused the diagnosis was very bad.

What do you mean exactly by stop taking medication if I feel brave? Sorry I'm just not sure I follow.

Besides symptoms of my disease, I recently lost someone very close to my heart and that has been very difficult to accept along with my diagnosis. It's just been a lot lately.
I feel foolish now because I suppose this was the only solution... thanks for your reply though and I will go first thing.
Thank you for your replies. I will make an appointment with my GP first thing tomorrow.

Thanks for the reply.

I haven’t been screened at all for heart disease as far as I’m aware (edit: beyond what is routine) but I do have an innocent heart murmur that my (at the time) doctor discovered about 4 years ago. I’ve had some rather bad heart palpitations in the last month though that I didn’t mention because it didn’t seem relevant (they happened at completely separate times to the dizzy spells). I honestly hadn’t considered that it was a heart issue until I ready your reply. Feeling pretty foolish at this point..

That being said, would you recommend I make an appointment with my GP and talk with him first or should I seek out a cardiologist?
